title: Binance Sets Aside $6.34 Billion After $6.3 Billion Hack, the Largest Crypto Theft Ever
excerpt: Attackers drained about $6.3 billion from Binance's hot wallets in roughly 20 minutes on Thursday, in what the exchange traced to a compromised engineer's laptop. Binance says customer balances will be restored one-for-one, $3 billion of the stolen assets have been frozen, and withdrawals are expected to resume by Sunday.
body:
• Binance has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company resources to restore customer balances after attackers stole an estimated $6.3 billion — the largest crypto theft in history.
  • The exchange says the attack began with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which let attackers submit unauthorised withdrawals from hot wallets across multiple blockchains in about 20 minutes; it found no evidence of a private-key leak.
  • About $3 billion of the stolen assets have been frozen by industry partners, and blockchain firms including TRM Labs and Chainalysis link the attack to North Korean hackers with high confidence.
  • Withdrawals remain paused pending security checks — the exchange expects them to resume by Sunday — while deposits remain open; Bitcoin fell below $77,000 and about $1.5 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated.

Binance said it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company resources to restore customer balances after attackers stole an estimated $6.3 billion from the world's largest crypto exchange, in the largest such theft in history, according to CoinDesk.

The exchange said $5 billion of the cover is already held in the exact token assets that were affected, so affected balances can be restored one-for-one without taking other customers' funds. Partners have separately frozen $3 billion in stolen assets. Binance is also drawing on its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), an emergency reserve that has typically held around $1 billion in bitcoin.

"Ultimately, all user funds will be verified publicly through our Proof of Reserves. We will weather this storm."

— Binance, in an update shared with CoinDesk

How the Money Left

Late on Thursday, attackers drained Binance's hot wallets across multiple blockchains in a burst lasting about 20 minutes. The haul included bitcoin, ether and the stablecoins USDT and USDC, among smaller tokens. According to blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, the attacker's wallets at one point held more than $5.7 billion, including nearly $1.5 billion in bitcoin, $900 million in ether, roughly $1.5 billion in USDT and over $800 million in USDC.

Binance's initial investigation points to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed the attacker to reach a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions. The exchange said it found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. Co-CEO Richard Teng said the attack was not a "one-click" action but a complex process, CNN reported, and co-CEO Yi He said on X that the platform would cover all hacking losses.

Blockchain analysis firms linked the exploit to North Korea with high confidence. TRM Labs traced the attack to "TraderTraitor," an elite North Korean hacking unit, saying several features match earlier North Korea-linked heists. Chainalysis put its estimate of the amount stolen at roughly $5.9 billion at the time of the theft and said it is tracking the funds moving across multiple blockchains. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze a large share of the stablecoins — about $2.6 billion between them on early tallies — within an hour of the attack.

The Market Reaction

Crypto prices fell sharply on the news, CoinDesk reported. Bitcoin dropped 4.8 percent to below $77,000 and ether fell 5.7 percent, while Binance's own BNB token dropped 8.7 percent in an hour. CoinGlass data showed about $1.55 billion in leveraged positions liquidated over 24 hours, hitting 239,610 traders. Binance held roughly $144 billion in assets on its platform before the hack, according to DefiLlama, so the stolen funds amount to about 4 percent of holdings. DefiLlama has recorded 322 confirmed crypto incidents in 2026 so far, with more than $8.7 billion in losses — this single theft is most of that total.

What Binance Users Should Know

Withdrawals remain paused while security checks are completed; the exchange expects withdrawal services to resume by Sunday morning, and deposits remain open. If you hold assets on Binance, no action is required for the promised one-for-one restoration, but do not move funds into the exchange until the withdrawal service is confirmed restored, and verify any communication claiming to be from Binance through the official app — large hacks are routinely followed by phishing campaigns impersonating support teams.

What's Next

The test of Binance's promise will be its next proof-of-reserves publication, which the exchange says will publicly verify restored balances. Investigators, meanwhile, are in a race standard to large heists: stolen coins are typically moved through bridges, decentralised trading venues and mixers within hours, and the $3 billion frozen so far is the portion issuers and partners reached first.
